findings.rationale: ExactToken.pull is an internal library primitive, not a public arbitrary-from entrypoint. Reviewed all production call sites: they pull from msg.sender, including BridgeRouter._fund whose private from parameter is supplied only with the authenticated caller. The receiving address is always the calling contract; sender and receiver balance deltas must both equal amount. Existing approvals cannot be spent by a caller naming an unrelated wallet. Exact-transfer/admitted-token trust is still a separate assumption.

There is no caller-selected unauthorized payout path.

findings.rationale: RewardReceiver.sync is nonReentrant and wrappedNative is immutable. beforeWrapped is an exact conversion postcondition: deposit must add exactly new native funds while protected native funds remain untouched. This does not prove a governance-admitted wrapper can never become malicious.

findings.rationale: returnFunds is nonReentrant, phase6-only and sets returned[slot][index] before the peer call. The peer returnFunding authenticates the immediate source, source phase6, destination phase7, prior incoming funding and that returned flag, then consumes incomingFunded before pushing exact captured funds. beforeBalance plus amount is the required post-transfer delta at the fixed source module. Callbacks cannot repeat the return or bypass the fixed source-module restore hook; a donation or shortfall causes atomic rejection.

findings.rationale: The beforeWrapped snapshot is intentionally the exact 1:1 wrapping invariant, not an authorization balance. canonicalSettle is only the fixed Fees contract, is nonReentrant, and marks the cutoff settled before the wrapper call. The fixed coordinator has already frozen every economic module and is itself nonReentrant. Nested wrapping/settlement cannot spend this cutoff twice; a non-exact wrapper output reverts that settlement call, leaving the captured source frozen for retry or abort. Wrapper liveness and truthful ERC20 balance reporting remain dependency admission risks, not a bypass of this balance check.

findings.rationale: settle is nonReentrant, accepts only phase8 and the exact next domain, and calls only sealed modules. All raw cutoffs were captured before phase8 became externally observable. Controller settling authority is enabled only for this call and disabled before advancing the cursor. Reentrant settle/export/fund/abort cannot cross the coordinator lock or phase checks. bindFrozen is importer-only phase4 and authenticates its paired source, so it cannot modify the settling source. Failure rolls back this domain and its cursor; success cannot replay.

findings.rationale: freeze is timelocked and nonReentrant, sets phase8/controller state1 before all observations, and captures all six domains without settling. Vault/Fees barriers reject an ingress callback freeze. Counts, export cursors and single-use funding flags are initialized under that lock; only a verified inert peer is bound.
